title: Check yourself: escapes in text blocks

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A text block line reads `INSERT INTO audit (id, note) \`, and the developer's editor left two spaces after the backslash, before the line break. What happens when the class is compiled?

options.text: The line is joined to the next one, since the trailing spaces are stripped before the backslash is read
options.says: javac checks each backslash as it reads the literal, before any stripping, so the spaces are still there

options.text: javac rejects the line as an illegal escape, since the trailing spaces are stripped before the backslash is read
options.says: had the spaces been stripped first, the backslash would end the line and be a valid continuation; the error comes because they are still there

options.text: javac rejects the line as an illegal escape, since the backslash is read while the spaces are still there
options.says: a backslash followed by a space is no escape, and javac checks it before trailing spaces are stripped

options.text: The line is joined to the next one, since the backslash is read while the spaces are still there
options.says: a backslash followed by a space starts no valid escape, so the file doesn't compile

origin.section: A Backslash at the End of a Line Removes the Line Break and Nothing Else

questions.stem: A code generator must put Python's docstring delimiter into a text block, and writes it as `\u0022\u0022\u0022` in the middle of a content line. What does javac do with that line?

options.text: It puts three quotes into the value, since the escapes become quotes only after javac has found the block's end
options.says: that holds for \" but not for unicode escapes, which are translated before javac reads the block at all

options.text: It ends the block in mid-line, since the escapes become quotes before javac looks for the block's end
options.says: unicode escapes are translated before the source is divided into tokens, so the line holds three ordinary quotes

options.text: It ends the block in mid-line, since the escapes become quotes only after javac has found the block's end
options.says: if they became quotes only afterwards, they could not close the block; they close it because they are translated first

options.text: It puts three quotes into the value, since the escapes become quotes before javac looks for the block's end
options.says: three quotes present when javac looks for the end form the closing delimiter, which javac reports as errors

origin.section: Unicode Escapes Are Translated Before the Compiler Sees the Text Block

questions.stem: Shop notices are loaded from a database table. One reads `Caf\u00e9 open\n9-17`, every backslash stored as a character, and the code calls `notice.translateEscapes()` on it. What comes out?

options.text: It returns Café open, a line break and 9-17, since Unicode escapes are among the escapes of a string literal
options.says: translateEscapes() leaves unicode escapes out: they belong to javac's reading of the source, not to the literal

options.text: It returns Café open, a line break and 9-17, since Unicode escapes are not among the escapes of a string literal
options.says: an escape the method doesn't accept makes it throw IllegalArgumentException, not pass through

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, since Unicode escapes are among the escapes of a string literal
options.says: the method accepts every escape of a literal; it throws on \u precisely because unicode escapes are not one of them

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, since Unicode escapes are not among the escapes of a string literal
options.says: translateEscapes() accepts only the escapes of a string literal; \u is not one, so it is a malformed escape

origin.section: translateEscapes() Interprets Escapes in a String That Arrives at Run Time

questions.stem: A team saves all its sources with CRLF line endings. A test compares a mail server's greeting, `220 ready` CR LF `250 OK` CR LF, with a text block holding those two lines, written without escapes and with the closing delimiter on its own line. Where does the test pass?

options.text: It fails everywhere, since javac turns the file's line endings into a line feed alone
options.says: javac turns every line terminator in a text block into LF before anything else; only \r puts a CR in the value

options.text: It passes everywhere, since the block keeps the line endings the file was saved with
options.says: every CR LF of the source file became a lone 0a in the value

options.text: It fails everywhere, since the block keeps the line endings the file was saved with
options.says: a block that kept the file's CR LF would match the greeting; it fails because the endings become LF

options.text: It passes everywhere, since javac turns the file's line endings into a line feed alone
options.says: LF alone doesn't match the server's CR LF, so the comparison fails

origin.section: Line Breaks in the Source Become \n Whatever the File Uses; Only an Escape Puts \r in the Value

concepts: Every line terminator of the source, CR LF included, is LF in a text block's value.
A space between a line-ending backslash and the line break is an illegal escape, reported before trailing spaces are stripped.
translateEscapes() interprets the escapes of a literal in a string read at run time and throws IllegalArgumentException on \u.
Unicode escapes are translated before the text block is read, so \u0022\u0022\u0022 closes it.
